newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Infrastructure funding seen as key to EU spat.
newsitem.headline: Infrastructure funding seen as key to EU spat.

text.p: The big problem for European Union leaders is to find a way of dealing with France's demands to resurrect funding for Trans-European Networks (TENs) as a way for creating jobs, an EU diplomat said on Sunday.
"Nobody wants to commit themselves to spending at this summit," he said. "To know exactly how to deal with (TENs) is the problem.

The diplomat dismissed the difficulty of getting agreement on resolutions attached to the stability pact, the bloc's framework for keeping deficits under control after economic and monetary union (EMU).

France has been demanding more attention be paid to employment issues in the run up to EMU and wants funding for major infrastructure programmes such as TENs, which have been agreed by the EU but not funded. TENs include large road, rail and telecommunications links between and within EU countries.
Germany has refused to countenance job-funding programmes.

The diplomat said he expected that EU finance ministers would not come up with a compromise at an informal dinner they plan on Sunday evening, but that they would use the occasion to get up to speed on the dispute following the Franco-German summit on Friday.

Asked whether there was concern about market reaction to a failure to agree at the EU summit on Monday, the diplomat noted that the French franc had fallen sharply for a while last Monday when France raised its questions about the stability pact.
"It was a useful reminder of who sets the tone on this," the diplomat said.
He added: "We might have a problem on our hands if this isn't resolved by late afternoon tomorrow (Monday)."
